I stored my Playwright tests in GitHub and configured GitHub Actions to start them automatically. The Playwright service URL tells the test runner which Azure Playwright Workspace to use for remote browser sessions. I created a Microsoft Entra app registration to provide an application identity, and its service principal received permission to use the Playwright Workspace. I configured a federated credential so only workflows from my specified GitHub repository and branch could authenticate as that application. During a run, GitHub generates a temporary OIDC token, Microsoft Entra verifies its repository details against the federated credential, and Azure issues a temporary access token. Azure RBAC then checks the service principal’s workspace permissions. Finally, because Playwright reporting writes artifacts to Azure Blob Storage, I assigned the same service principal the Storage Blob Data Contributor role on the linked storage account.
